newsitem.title: THAILAND: Dlr unwinding eases Thai repo rates-BOT official.
newsitem.headline: Dlr unwinding eases Thai repo rates-BOT official.

text.p: A liquidity squeeze in the currency market prompted commercial banks to raise short-term baht funds by selling dollars to the Bank of Thailand, assistant central bank governor Siri Ganjarerndee said on Thursday.
Siri told reporters the central bank-run Exchange Equalisation Fund was offered to buy a sharply higher amount of U.S. dollars from commercial banks on Thursday.
He said easier liquidity stemming from the central bank's injection helped push its one-day repo rate to 8.875 percent in late afternoon from 14.25 percent at the morning close.
The official said the central bank welcomed the baht's growing stability on Thursday after joint intervention by Thai and Singapore central banks to defend the baht a day earlier.
"Cooperation among regional central banks is essential as currency speculators work the same way as stock speculators," he said.
The baht was quoted sharply firmer at 25.200/25.400 to the dollar late on Thursday against 25.910/25.940 early in the morning and 26.330/26.430 late on Wednesday.
